overview: This file consists of a single State Department cross-reference sheet directing researchers to telegram no. 1181 in file 311.114-Liquor/901. The referenced communication, sent from Japan by U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew on February 21, 1935, concerned Japanese wine labeling and reported that Japan did not issue certificates attesting a product’s character, place of origin, or legality of manufacture.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Japan; sender of the referenced telegram

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Grew telegram on Japanese wine labeling
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to telegram no. 1181 concerning wine labeling and the absence of Japanese product-certification documents.
subfiles.summary: This document-file note cross-references telegram no. 1181, filed under 311.114-Liquor/901. It identifies the communication as originating in Japan from Grew on February 21, 1935. The note states that Japan did not issue certificates attesting the character, place of origin, and legality of manufacture of its products.

interest: The sheet is useful as evidence of the State Department’s decimal-file cross-referencing practices and as a pointer to the substantive telegram in another file. Its brief description also highlights a practical obstacle in regulating or documenting Japanese wine imports: the apparent absence of official Japanese certificates concerning character, origin, and lawful manufacture.
